name: boat

attributes.attribute: linked to the Celtic goddess of waters
site of a goddess sculpture holding a cornucopia on a boat
Roman goddess also associated with these symbols
may link Celtic fertility and Roman abundance

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The boat is a symbolic object. It links to the Celtic goddess of waters. Sculptures from the Roman period show this. An unnamed goddess at Nuits-Saint-Georges in France holds a cornucopia. She stands on the prow and rudder of a boat. Those symbols also belong to the Roman goddess Fortuna. The boat may join fertility and abundance. The Celts tied fertility to waters feeding the land. The Romans saw abundance as fortune. See Nehalennia.

okr.objective: Describe the boat as a symbol of the Celtic goddess of waters.
